brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;half-n + piece:0,0,1;half-n and piece:1,0,0;full + piece:1,0,1;full create 2 levels (level 0 and level 1)

16 caps placed (cap:0,0,0;*;150,30,90 etc. and cap:1,0,1;*). 2 faces remain open 1,0,0;*;90 and 1,0,0;*;150 — configurator refuses with MESH_CLASH into hex-drawer-frame-s (5mm > 0.5 limit), check_build reports OPEN_CAP_FACE info only, meshClash clear

finish.summary: Build has two storeys with two bins on upper level and drawer on lower level. 16 of 18 open edges capped; final 2 lower-level edges adjacent to drawer clash with drawer frame and cannot be capped per configurator mesh rules. check_build ok, meshClash clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text:
Two storey workbench organizer configured: level0 + level1 with two cells. Bins on upper storey placed. Drawer on lower half base. Caps placed on all open edges that the configurator allows. One lower half-north face (270°) is capped via # face cap; top storey fully capped. Remaining lower edges noted as clashes.

**Note on caps:** caps at `1,0,0;*;90` and `1,0,0;*;150` were offered but refused with MESH_CLASH (hex-cap-edge-solid-f into hex-drawer-frame-s, 5mm). This is a system enforced limit, not omitted.
